title: Avian taxi drivers? A commentary on ‘Diversity of fungi attached to birds corresponds to the habitat ecologies of their avian dispersal vectors’
content: Birds are increasingly recognized not only as seed dispersers, but also as important agents of fungal dispersal. Although their role in seed dispersal, particularly through frugivory, has been studied extensively owing to its significance for long-distance dispersal and forest regeneration (Spiegel and Nathan, 2007), their role in transporting fungi has received comparatively little attention. Early work by Heald and Studhalter (1913) documented birds dispersing plant pathogenic fungi such as Cryphonectria parasitica, the causative agent of chestnut blight. However, research on bird–fungal interactions has lagged behind that of bird–plant relationships. Recent findings suggest that avian-mediated fungal dispersal is far more widespread and ecologically important than previously recognized (for a comprehensive review, see Elliott et al., 2019). Despite this growing recognition, the diversity of fungi dispersed by birds and the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly understood.
